detail.longDescription: I am building a plugin framework where child models are dynamically instantiated and mixed with a base configuration class using __init_subclass__ . Everything works as expected when using standard dataclasses. However, as soon as I enable slots=True (introduced in Python 3.10+) on both the base and mixin classes, Python throws a TypeError: multiple bases have instance lay-out conflict during class creation. from dataclasses import dataclass # Base mixin containing shared tracking state @dataclass(slots=True) class ServiceMixin: service_id: str # Base entity dataclass @dataclass(slots=True) class BaseEntity: entity_id: int # Child class inheriting from both base classes @dataclass(slots=True) class UserEntity(BaseEntity, ServiceMixin): username: str Error: Traceback (most recent call last): File "main.py", line 14, in <module> class UserEntity(BaseEntity, ServiceMixin): TypeError: multiple bases have instance lay-out conflict I tried: Removing slots=True from child or parents. If I set slots=False on ServiceMixin , the exception goes away, but UserEntity falls back to creating a standard __dict__ , which defeats the memory optimization goal. Reordering the base classes. Changing the MRO to class UserEntity(ServiceMixin, BaseEntity) yields the exact same error. Defining empty __slots__ = () manually. If I define ServiceMixin without @dataclass(slots=True) and manually set __slots__ = ('service_id',) or __slots__ = () , the behavior changes unpredictably depending on which parent class declares non-empty slots. How can I safely apply slots=True across multiple inherited dataclasses without triggering CPython's layout conflict restriction? Is there an idiomatic pattern or workaround (e.g., via a helper mixin or metaclass) to allow slot-based multiple inheritance in dataclasses?
